sam: can you paste the exact request_id + the client's timestamp and the curl they used? also which customer/org?

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
```

jordan: if Kibana search for request_id returns nothing, try searching both request_id and trace.id across indices. example KQL: 

```
request_id:"req_9f1b2c3d" OR trace.id:"9f1b2c3d"
```

also check edge logs with `edge.request_id:req_9f1b2c3d` (edge and upstream sometimes have different ids).

kyle: FYI retention: hot indices ~30d, cold indices ~90d. If the event is older than 30d it may live in cold-* or S3 archive. Archive pulls take 24-72h and require an export request.

ingest-bot: automated note: logs older than 30 days may be moved to cold storage or S3 archive. Use /tools/log-export {request_id, time_window, org} to request retrieval. Expected turnaround 24-48h for cold index, 48-72h for S3 archive.

maya: customer says it's intermittent and they can reproduce. asked them to run curl with verbose headers and capture response body. suggested this repro curl that sets an x-debug header so server emits extra traces (will only work in non-prod where header is allowed):

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Debug-Mode: true" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_9f1b2c3d" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":["test"]}' -v
```

ask them to attach the full curl -v output and the raw response JSON. also asked them to generate a debug-bundle (link: https://internal.redwood.tools/debug-bundle) and include the client headers and exact wallclock time.

sam: I can run a raw-grep across the raw edge logs if you confirm the exact minute. @kyle can you pre-authorize a cold fetch for req_9f1b2c3d if we don't find it in hot indices? I'll try a few patterns: `req_9f1b2c3d`, `9f1b2c3d`, and the client's IP if provided.

kyle: pre-authorized. if we need an S3 archive pull I'll open the zendesk with tag `log-retrieve` and link back here. also: when searching, use this expanded KQL to catch variations: 

```
(request_id:"req_9f1b2c3d" OR trace.id:"9f1b2c3d" OR message:/9f1b2c3d/) and @timestamp:["2026-03-16T22:00:00" TO "2026-03-16T22:20:00"]
```

kyle: note = if we hit the archive path, include the service shard (edge/ingest/runner) from the debug bundle to narrow the S3 key.

maya: customer will send the debug bundle and the verbose curl output in this thread. i'll post the bundle link once they upload. :thumbsup:

kyle: logging tip for future: ask customers to include an `X-Request-ID` header (client-generated) and `User-Agent` string so we can correlate earlier in the pipeline (edge logs usually keep client UA).

maya: adding that to our repro checklist. closing the loop once the bundle is in.
